subtopics.title: The Atmosphere — Composition, Structure and Heating

questions.question: The two most abundant gases in the atmosphere are:
options: Nitrogen at about 78 per cent and oxygen at about 21 per cent
Oxygen at about 78 per cent and carbon dioxide at about 21 per cent
Carbon dioxide and water vapour
Argon and ozone

questions.question: Temperature rises with height in the stratosphere because:
options: It sits closest to the sun
The ozone layer there absorbs ultraviolet radiation and warms the surrounding air
Greenhouse gases collect there
Meteors burn up in that layer

questions.question: The air is heated from below means that:
options: Volcanic heat warms the lower atmosphere
Warm ocean currents heat the whole atmosphere
Sunlight mostly passes through air, warms the surface, and the surface then warms the air on it
The earth's core radiates heat into the air

questions.question: The four processes that move heat through the atmosphere are:
options: Insolation, rotation, revolution, reflection
Melting, freezing, boiling, condensing
Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff
Radiation, conduction, convection and advection

subtopics.title: Moisture, Clouds and the Three Rainfall Types

questions.question: Relative humidity is:
options: The vapour in the air expressed as a percentage of the maximum that air at that temperature could carry
The mass of vapour in a cubic metre of air
The temperature at which condensation begins
The percentage of days with rain

questions.question: Dew point is the temperature at which:
options: Water begins to evaporate
Frost always forms
Rain begins to fall
Cooling air reaches saturation — 100 per cent relative humidity

questions.question: The cloud that signals thunder, hail and violent rain is:
options: Cirrus
The anvil-headed cumulonimbus
Stratus
Fair-weather cumulus

questions.question: Matching rainfall types to South African addresses:
options: Frontal rain over the Free State; convectional rain in Cape Town's winter
Orographic rain only at the coast; frontal rain over the Karoo
Convectional summer storms over the interior; orographic rain on windward mountain slopes; frontal winter rain in the south-western Cape
All three types occur only in summer

subtopics.title: The Restless Crust — Plates, Folds, Faults and Quakes

questions.question: Wegener's evidence for continental drift included:
options: Satellite measurements of plate speeds
Ocean temperature records
The magnetic striping of the sea floor
The jigsaw fit of continents, matching fossils like Mesosaurus and Glossopteris, matching rock layers, and glacial scars in warm lands

questions.question: Where an oceanic plate meets a continental plate at a convergent boundary:
options: The denser oceanic plate subducts beneath, melting to feed volcanic chains like the Andes
Both plates rise into fold mountains
A mid-ocean ridge forms
The plates slide past without effect

questions.question: A graben, such as the East African Rift Valley, forms when:
options: Lava builds a broad shield
Two anticlines collide
A block of crust drops between two parallel faults
A block is thrust upward between faults

questions.question: Magnitude and Mercalli intensity differ in that:
options: Both give one identical number per quake
Magnitude measures energy released, one number per quake; Mercalli measures observed effects, varying from place to place
Mercalli is read by instruments; magnitude by observers
Magnitude applies only to volcanoes

subtopics.title: Mapwork Essentials — Scale, Contours, Gradient and the Synoptic Chart

questions.question: On a 1:50 000 topographic map:
options: 1 centimetre represents 50 kilometres
5 centimetres represent 1 kilometre
The scale changes with the terrain
2 centimetres represent 1 kilometre, and the contour interval is 20 metres

questions.question: Magnetic declination is:
options: The angle between true north and magnetic north, printed on the sheet with its annual change
The difference between two contour lines
The tilt of the earth's axis
The error in a poorly drawn map

questions.question: Where contours cross a river valley, the V shape they form points:
options: Downstream, toward the sea
Upstream, into the high ground
Always due north
Toward the nearest summit

questions.question: Two points differ by 160 metres in height and lie 2 400 metres apart. The gradient is:
options: 1 in 8
1 in 15
1 in 24

subtopics.title: The Tar Road at Noon — Air, Heat and Rain Made Simple

questions.question: The shimmer above a hot tar road demonstrates:
options: Air warmed by the hot surface rising in convection — heating from below
Sunlight heating the air directly
Advection from the coast
The greenhouse effect in action

questions.question: The cold cooldrink can sweats in warm air because:
options: The can leaks slowly through its seams
Metal attracts water vapour magnetically
The drink inside evaporates through the metal
Air chilled against the can passes its dew point, and its vapour condenses into droplets

questions.question: The blanket and the sunscreen must not be swapped because:
options: Both are names for the ozone layer
Greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat, while the ozone layer blocks incoming ultraviolet — different layers, different jobs
Both are found in the mesosphere
The blanket blocks ultraviolet and the sunscreen traps heat

subtopics.title: The Dry Mud Pan — Plates, Folds and Faults Made Simple

questions.question: In the dried mud pan picture of the earth, the cracked plates rest on:
options: The planet's liquid core
A layer of compressed sand
Softer, slowly creeping hot rock whose currents carry the plates along
Solid unbroken granite

questions.question: The rug and the ruler stand for:
options: Rock bending slowly into folds, against rock snapping suddenly along a fault
Two kinds of volcanic eruption
Continental and oceanic crust
Erosion and deposition

questions.question: The epicentre of an earthquake is:
options: The underground point where the rock gave way
The fault line's deepest segment
The zone that suffers no shaking
The point on the surface directly above the focus, where shaking usually peaks

questions.question: One quake, one magnitude, many intensities summarises that:
options: Every town measures its own magnitude
The energy released is a single instrument-read number, while observed effects differ from place to place
Magnitude changes as the quake travels
Intensity is always larger than magnitude

subtopics.title: The Dam in a Drought — Mapwork Rehearsed Out Loud

questions.question: The watermarks left on a dam's banks as the level falls behave like contours because each ring:
options: Joins all points that stood at exactly the same height
Shows where the water is deepest
Marks one month of drought
Points toward the dam wall

questions.question: In the spoken gradient routine, 160 metres of rise over 4.8 centimetres of map distance on a 1:50 000 sheet gives:
options: 1 in 30, because 4 800 divided by 160 is 30
1 in 48, using the map distance directly
2 400 metres of ground distance, and 2 400 over 160 equals 15 — a gradient of 1 in 15
1 in 160, using the height difference

questions.question: On a station model, the wind shaft:
options: Points toward where the wind is going
Shows the temperature gradient
Circles the station when winds are calm
Sticks out toward where the wind comes from, with feathers counting speed in knots

questions.question: As a cold front passes the Cape, the scorecard flips to:
options: Wind veering south-west, temperature falling, pressure climbing, showers then clearing
Wind backing north, temperature rising, pressure falling steadily
Calm winds and rising temperature
No measurable change at the surface
